findings.title: The interrogative presents denial for judgment
findings.claim: The third “gördün mü” question turns the condition of denying and turning away into a case placed before the addressee for evaluation, before the passage's divine-seeing answer.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier أَرَءَيْتَ addresses the interlocutor with a request for attention and judgment. Its contact with the exact interrogative parallels at 6:40 and 107:1, together with the watchfulness contact at 89:14, changes the question from bare visual report into accountable recognition of conduct.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear “gördün mü” as a summons to acknowledge what the denial-and-turning posture means, not only as a request to look at a scene.
findings.containment: The plain conditional “Gördün mü, ya yalanlayıp yüz çevirdiyse?” remains intact. This finding does not supply the final divine verdict or resolve whether the conditional subjects are identical across the surrounding ayat.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication anchors the focus question and its judgment relation; the reader-walk corroboration and target-side morphology remain qualified by the packet boundary.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The 6:40 connection stages accountable recognition through the same question family, while 89:14 supplies divine watchfulness as the horizon of scrutiny.
branch_activations.activation: The interrogative carrier meets question-and-watchfulness contacts that make the following denial and turning an object of considered judgment.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The ayah presents the opponent's conduct as something the addressee is asked to assess before the next divine-seeing response.
branch_activations.boundary: The judgment facet does not itself state the final verdict or replace the ordinary request to see and consider.

branch_activations.boundary: This does not claim that the question alone proves a divine judgment or that the parallel ayah supplies missing morphology for the focus.

findings.title: Denial becomes an exposed bodily quality
findings.claim: كَذَّبَ establishes an active repudiation of a truth claim, and the later sequence can expose that repudiation as a bodily and public quality attached to the forelock.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier كَذَّبَ is an objectless Form II act of declaring false. Its contact with the fabrication-and-signs relation at 10:17 and the denial-after-exposure relation at 20:56 gives the act an outward target; the supplied 96:16 continuation makes the act's falsehood visible at the rejecter's front.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees denial as an enacted cancellation whose trace can become attached to the denier, rather than as a detached opinion that disappears after being spoken.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains “yalanlayıp.” 96:13 does not itself name the forelock, and this continuation does not settle the identity of the conditional subject or erase the live counter-speech reading.

epistemic.reason: A trusted cross-run finding supplies the focus denial relation, while the reader-walk material supplies the later bodily continuation with legacy provenance.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Doğruluğa aykırılık hem söylenen bir sözde hem de yapılan bir davranışta gerçekleşebilir.
branch_activations.carrier: The objectless Form II carrier كَذَّبَ marks an outward act of treating a truth-bearing claim as false.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The exact 10:17 connection pairs fabrication against God with denial of signs.
branch_activations.activation: The denial carrier meets a fabrication-and-signs contact, so falsehood functions as an active posture toward an external claim.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The ayah's denial reads as an enacted falsification that can be traced to the person who performs it.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not turn every available falsehood branch into the focus meaning or add an unstated object to the verb.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kişi veya söz, yalan olduğu söylenerek doğruluk bakımından olumsuz değerlendirilir.
branch_activations.carrier: The same كَذَّبَ carrier actively judges a person or claim to be false rather than merely reporting an untrue utterance.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The 20:56 connection places denial after all signs have been displayed, and the supplied later records attach كاذبة to the forelock.
branch_activations.activation: The act of declaring false meets a context in which exposure does not end refusal and a later adjective makes the falsehood publicly bodily.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The conditional denial opens onto an enduring, visible description of the one who performs it.
branch_activations.boundary: The later forelock description is a contextual continuation, not a claim that the noun is grammatically present in 96:13.

findings.title: Denial can construct a rival account
findings.claim: The denial can also be heard as an attempt to construct a false verbal account against the claim being examined, giving the refusal the shape of counter-speech.
findings.mechanism: The focus كَذَّبَ carrier supplies the act of declaring false. Its contact with the fabrication pairing at 10:17 and the conjectural denial pattern at 6:148 lets the refusal operate as a rival account rather than only a private judgment about truth.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive how denial contests the account under examination: it does not merely withdraw assent, it presents a competing story as though it could cancel the claim.
findings.containment: The plain “yalanladı” reading remains primary. This is a qualified counter-speech resonance, not an assertion that 96:13 contains a separate fabrication verb or that the rival account is the only force of كَذَّبَ.

epistemic.reason: The citable publication is marked weak and the connection targets lack focus-side morphology, so the counter-speech mechanism remains bounded while its carrier and contacts are explicit.

findings.title: Denial and turning form one enacted course
findings.claim: The conditional scene joins the attention-demanding question, active denial, and turning away into one course of conduct whose withdrawal can also open toward a socially backed rival direction.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers أَرَءَيْتَ, كَذَّبَ, and تَوَلَّىٰ meet exact question, fabrication/repudiation, alliance, and paired-refusal contacts. Their contacts make the three operations explain one another as a movement from being asked to recognize, through repudiation, into turning away; the authority facet is retained as a qualified social extension.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees “yalanlayıp yüz çevirdiyse” as an enacted trajectory rather than two disconnected labels, while the question keeps that trajectory before judgment.
findings.containment: The plain conditional remains recoverable throughout. The social-authority extension is bounded and does not make a council, rival rule, or single subject identity the only reading; the nominated fabricating-speech branch is excluded for lack of a carrier.

epistemic.reason: The reader-walk source is legacy and one nominated branch lacks a registered carrier, while the focus-mapped core has exact connection contacts and is retained with explicit qualification.

findings.title: Turning away reverses an available direction
findings.claim: تَوَلَّىٰ becomes an enacted reversal from the direction of return: its ordinary withdrawal remains in place, while the toward-and-facing field makes the abandoned orientation perceptible.
findings.mechanism: The focus turning carrier meets the supplied return-and-guidance contrast and connections that set turning away against protection and make it embodied. The exact paired refusal at 92:16 and the visible withdrawal at 80:1 make the directional reversal materially different from a mood of indifference.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel “yüz çevirmek” as a change of course with a recoverable before-direction, not only as disappearance from a scene.
findings.containment: The ordinary objectless withdrawal is primary and remains recoverable. The toward/facing facet is a contextual contrast that names the direction being abandoned; it does not make turning toward the local grammatical sense or settle the subject.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication anchors the reversal relation, while the directional contrast is supplied through legacy reader-walk evidence and connection targets whose morphology is not supplied.

branch_activations.boundary: This does not add disappearance, authority, or a uniquely identified actor to the ordinary withdrawal.

findings.title: Withdrawal can open toward rival authority
findings.claim: The turning can extend beyond leaving the scene into a socially backed reorientation, where withdrawing from the prior direction opens toward taking charge of another allegiance.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier تَوَلَّىٰ meets alliance and intermediary-allegiance contacts at 9:23 and 39:3, while the supplied reader-walk evidence attributes later council mobilization to the same turn. The paired-refusal contact at 92:16 keeps the authority extension attached to the ordinary withdrawal.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive how “yüz çevirmek” may become the first movement of self-authorized alignment, rather than merely a person stepping out of view.
findings.containment: Withdrawal remains the recoverable primary reading and the alliance contact is a qualified extension. This does not make rival authority the only meaning, assert a fully formed political rule, or resolve the conditional subject.

epistemic.reason: The trusted finding supplies the authority consequence, while legacy walk material supplies the later mobilization and the target connections provide secondary alliance contacts.

branch_activations.boundary: The authority branch is a qualified extension of the focus form; it does not replace the ordinary sense of turning away.

branch_activations.boundary: The connection preserves the joined course but does not itself prove a unique authority outcome.
